config.title: useRef Typing

intro.title: useRef Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses a typed reference to access a DOM element directly. You will learn the core concept of creating and using typed references in Angular to interact with HTML elements without relying on template variables. The main technologies involved are Angular's ElementRef and TypeScript's type annotations for ensuring type safety. By the end, you'll understand how to properly type a reference to manipulate DOM elements like changing text content or styles.
intro.usecase: In Angular applications, typed references are essential for managing DOM elements in complex interactive interfaces. For example, when building data dashboards with dynamic charts, developers use typed references to directly access and manipulate chart canvas elements for real-time updates. This pattern also appears in form validation scenarios where input fields need focus management after errors, or in custom dropdown menus that require precise control over opening/closing animations. By properly typing these references, developers ensure type safety while implementing responsive, interactive features that users encounter daily in enterprise applications.

objectives: Initialize a typed useRef hook to store DOM element references
Apply TypeScript generics to define the specific element type for useRef
Bind the ref attribute to Angular template elements with proper typing
Manipulate DOM element properties through the typed useRef current property
Integrate useRef with Angular lifecycle hooks for safe DOM access
Configure useRef to store mutable values while maintaining type safety
Implement conditional logic that checks the current property of a typed useRef

steps.title: Import Component and ElementRef from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component and ElementRef from '@angular/core' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in both symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing Angular core symbols
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component and ElementRef from '@angular/core' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core imports are added, enabling component creation and template reference typing.
successCriteria: Component and ElementRef are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure to import both Component and ElementRef from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import Component and ElementRef from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a class named UseRefTypingComponent and decorate it with @Component.
steps.hint: Define a TypeScript class with the name UseRefTypingComponent and add the @Component decorator above it.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, ElementRef } from '@angular/core';

// Create the UseRefTypingComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class is defined with proper TypeScript syntax and the @Component decorator.
successCriteria: A class named UseRefTypingComponent exists and is decorated with @Component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class is named UseRefTypingComponent and has the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incorrect. Check the class name and @Component decorator.

steps.title: Add template and styles to component metadata
steps.instruction: Inside the @Component decorator, add a template property with a simple heading and a styles property with basic CSS.
steps.hint:
Add template: '

' and styles: ['h1 { color: blue; }'] to the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component metadata now includes a template with a heading and basic styling.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator has both template and styles properties with valid values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some properties, but make sure both template and styles are present with correct syntax.

steps.title: Declare ElementRef property with proper typing
steps.instruction: Inside the UseRefTypingComponent class, add a property named 'inputRef' with type 'ElementRef<HTMLInputElement>'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body with the correct type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has a typed template reference property ready to be used with an input element.
successCriteria: The 'inputRef' property is declared with type 'ElementRef<HTMLInputElement>' in the component class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check the type annotation. It should be 'ElementRef<HTMLInputElement>'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property declaration is missing or incorrect. Add 'inputRef: ElementRef<HTMLInputElement>;' inside the component class.

steps.title: Inject ElementRef in constructor
steps.instruction: Add a constructor to the UseRefTypingComponent class that injects an ElementRef parameter and assigns it to the inputRef property you declared earlier.
steps.hint: In Angular, you can inject dependencies like ElementRef through the constructor. Use the private keyword to automatically assign the parameter to a class property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a constructor that properly injects ElementRef, making it available for template reference manipulation.
successCriteria: Constructor is added with ElementRef parameter injected and assigned to inputRef property
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your constructor has a parameter of type ElementRef and assigns it to the inputRef property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor injection isn't quite right. Remember to add a constructor with an ElementRef parameter and assign it to the inputRef property.

steps.title: Create a method to access the native element
steps.instruction: Inside the UseRefTypingComponent class, create a method named 'focusInput' that calls 'this.inputRef.nativeElement.focus()'.
steps.hint: Add a method within the class body, using the 'this' keyword to access the inputRef property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can programmatically focus the input element when called.
successCriteria: A method named 'focusInput' is defined in the component class and contains 'this.inputRef.nativeElement.focus()'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a method, but it doesn't fully match the expected implementation. Make sure it calls 'this.inputRef.nativeElement.focus()'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a method named 'focusInput' inside the class that accesses the native element.

steps.title: Add input element to template
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add an <input> element with a placeholder attribute set to 'Type something...'.
steps.hint: Look for the template property in the @Component decorator. Add the <input> element there.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains an <input> element that users can interact with.
successCriteria: The template includes an <input> element with a placeholder attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure it has a placeholder attribute like 'Type something...'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain an <input> element. Check the @Component decorator's template property.

steps.title: Add template reference variable to input
steps.instruction: Add a template reference variable named #inputElement to the <input> element in your component's template.
steps.hint: In Angular, template reference variables are created using the # symbol followed by a name, placed directly on an HTML element in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: template reference variable on a button -->
<button #myButton>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element in the template will have a template reference variable that can be used to reference it from other parts of the template or component.
successCriteria: The <input> element includes the #inputElement template reference variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added #inputElement directly on the <input> element in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template reference variable was not added correctly. Check that you've placed #inputElement on the <input> element.

steps.title: Add button element to template
steps.instruction: Add a <button> element with the text 'Focus Input' to the template, right after the existing <input> element.
steps.hint: Place the button element on a new line after the input element in the template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains both an input element and a button element with the text 'Focus Input'.
successCriteria: A <button> element with the text 'Focus Input' is added to the template after the <input> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Focus Input' and is placed after the input element in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with text 'Focus Input' is missing or incorrectly placed. Check that it's inside the template string after the input.

steps.title: Wire button click to focus method
steps.instruction: Add a (click) event binding to the button element in your template to call the focusInput() method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (event)="handler()". For a button click, the event is 'click'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a method
<button (click)="doSomething()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have a (click) event binding that triggers the focusInput() method when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element includes (click)="focusInput()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct event binding syntax (click)="focusInput()" on the button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button click isn't properly wired to the focusInput() method. Remember to use Angular's (event)="handler()" syntax for event binding.
